feature.title: The week in review: a Nvidia surge, a Dell blowout and a four-point intraday swing
body: **Monday:** Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang and the stock surged about 31%; the S&P 500 rose 4.73% and the Nasdaq 6.51%. **Tuesday:** chip stocks fell back, the Dow closed above 50,000 and the Nasdaq fell 1.48%. After the close Dell reported record revenue of $54.9 billion and a $132.3 billion AI backlog.

**Wednesday:** October PCE came in hot, with core at 3.3% against 3.2% expected, and the Nasdaq fell more than 4% at its low before recovering to a small loss. **Thursday:** US markets were closed for Thanksgiving.

By my arithmetic from closing levels, through Wednesday the S&P 500 is up about 3.9% on the week, the Nasdaq about 4.3% and the Dow about 4.2%, from last Friday's closes. Today's half-day close is not in these figures. The interview line: 'The week was about leadership and inflation: one stock's headline moved the market, and a hot PCE nearly broke it.'

stories.headline: Stocks rally in the Black Friday half-day as chips lead; Dow reported up about 1.2%, final closes unconfirmed
stories.dek: The premarket jump held into the shortened session, with semiconductors the leaders. I could not verify final index levels, so treat the percentages as reported.
stories.updateNote: Added the Friday session and corrected the Nvidia rating claim.
tldr: One report has the Dow up about **1.2%** to roughly 50,775 in the half-day; I could not confirm final closes for the S&P 500 or Nasdaq, which were up strongly.
Chips led: the premarket moves in Nvidia and Micron were the story, and one report put the Philadelphia chip index up more than 4%.
Correction: my morning edition said S&P Global put Nvidia's rating on negative watch. I could not confirm that; the verified action is Moody's (see the Nvidia brief).
whatHappened: The futures jump described this morning carried into the cash session. Reports from the half-day put the Dow up about 1.2% to roughly 50,775, which is consistent with Wednesday's close of 50,182.95, as Thursday was a holiday. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq also rose sharply, led by chip stocks, but I could not verify their final levels, so I am not quoting them. A single report put the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up more than 4%.

Earlier this morning, a single report said S&P Global Ratings had put Nvidia's AA rating on negative [[credit outlook]] watch. Follow-up searches found no such action. What is verified is Moody's: it affirmed Nvidia's Aa1 rating on Nov. 18 and cut the outlook to stable from positive. This edition fixes the earlier wording.
background: The rebound follows a violent Wednesday in which the Nasdaq fell more than 4% at its low before recovering. Futures traded through Thursday's holiday and reflect positioning, not a full market. A gain this size in a half-day session shows how much of Wednesday's selling was forced.
Chip stocks are the swing factor. Korea's memory makers and Nvidia move together, which is why SK Hynix and Micron led. The Taiwan dip is a reminder that not every chip name benefits equally.
whyItMatters: A shortened Friday session magnifies moves because there are fewer buyers and sellers. If the gap holds into the 1:00 PM close, it supports the case that Wednesday's low was a washout; if it fades, the AI group is still fragile into December's Fed meeting. The rating-watch report, if confirmed, adds a governance angle to Nvidia's rebound.

grandLine.title: The Log Pose
grandLine.body: A Log Pose only points to the next island after it has stayed on this one long enough to record it. Friday's gap up is a reading, not yet a heading: the half-day session is too short for the needle to settle. Monday, with a full day of trading, is when the Log Pose will really point.

views.thesis: A 2% to 3% gap after the worst of the selling means buyers are back.
views.argument: Nvidia, Micron and the Korean chipmakers all rallied, and Wednesday's low was a full-day reversal. With the Fed's decision still two weeks away, the path of least resistance is up into year-end.

views.thesis: Half-day sessions flatter moves and fade.
views.argument: Volume is low, the rating warning and chip-export worries are unresolved, and a hot PCE keeps a December hike nearly priced. A gap up on thin volume often reverses on Monday.

interview.question: The Nasdaq swung about 4 points on Wednesday and then rallied on a half-day. How do you read a move like that on thin volume?
interview.answer: I'd be cautious. A big move on low volume says less than the same move on a full day, because fewer participants are setting the price. The reason is that holiday sessions skip the institutional flow that gives a rally conviction. I'd change my mind if Monday's full session holds the gains on normal volume.

followUp.question: What do you do with a claim you can't confirm?
followUp.answer: Flag it, don't trade it, and correct it publicly if it turns out wrong. A rating action is a primary-source fact: you can check it with the agency.

keyTerms.definition: A rating agency's view of where a company's rating is likely to go over the next 12 to 24 months: positive, stable or negative.
keyTerms.example: Moody's moved Nvidia's outlook to stable from positive, so an upgrade is no longer expected soon.

stories.headline: Correction: Moody's, not S&P, acted on Nvidia: Aa1 affirmed, outlook cut to stable from positive
stories.dek: This morning's edition cited an unconfirmed S&P watch. The verified action is Moody's, on Nov. 18, citing the exit of Jensen Huang.
tldr: Moody's affirmed Nvidia's Aa1 rating on Nov. 18 and moved the outlook to stable from positive.
Moody's cited strategy uncertainty and no formal succession plan; I found no S&P Global action.
whatHappened: After the close on Nov. 18, Moody's affirmed Nvidia's Aa1 senior unsecured rating and cut the outlook to stable from positive. Reports say Moody's cited uncertainty after Jensen Huang's exit and the lack of a formal succession plan. Sources disagree on the date of his departure (Nov. 11 or 12).
The earlier claim that S&P Global put the rating on negative watch could not be confirmed in follow-up searches, so I am withdrawing it.
whyItMatters: The rating is still very high, so this is not a funding problem. A stable outlook means an upgrade is no longer expected soon. It also shows that governance, not earnings, is the open question for Nvidia, and the next signals are the CEO choice and the board's investigation.

stories.headline: OPEC+ meets Sunday for the bigger test: 2027 output quotas, after a third straight hold
stories.dek: The group held December targets on Nov. 1 while Gulf producers pumped below quota because of the Iran war. Analysts called Sunday's meeting the harder call.
tldr: On Nov. 1, seven core OPEC+ members kept December output targets unchanged for a third month.
Many Gulf producers are still below their quotas because of Iran war disruption; Sunday's meeting is expected to take up 2027 quotas and a capacity review.
whatHappened: On Nov. 1, seven core OPEC+ members, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, kept their December production targets unchanged in an online meeting, the third straight hold. Reports say many Gulf producers are still pumping below their quotas because of disruption from the Iran war, even as exports through the Strait of Hormuz have risen.

One analyst called that decision the easy one and said the bigger test comes at the Nov. 29 meeting, when the group has to negotiate 2027 quotas. A capacity review has to be finished before the end of the year. I could not find a verified preview of what is expected on Sunday.
whyItMatters: Oil is the input cost behind inflation, which is why the Fed's December decision matters. A quota deal that adds supply would ease that pressure; a hold with Gulf output still disrupted keeps it. Monday's oil open is the first read.
